title: Two by Two, at God's Command

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Pairs of clean and unclean animals, of birds and of all creatures that move along the ground, male and female, came to Noah and entered the ark, as God had commanded Noah. - Gen 7:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a quietly remarkable detail. Noah did not have to go out and hunt down every animal, chase the birds, or round up the creatures of the earth. The text says they "came to Noah and entered the ark." God brought them. Two by two, the animals came, moving into the place of safety exactly as God had arranged. What Noah could never have accomplished on his own, God did for him.

This shows us how God works to accomplish His purposes. When God has a plan, He also provides the means to carry it out. Noah's task was to build the ark and obey; it was God's task to bring the animals. God does not call us to a work and then leave us to manage the impossible parts alone. He goes before us and arranges what we cannot.

How often we exhaust ourselves trying to control outcomes that only God can bring about! We strive and worry over things far beyond our reach. But the God who brought the animals to the ark is the God who still moves circumstances, opens doors, and provides what His purposes require.

Our part is to trust and obey; God's part is to accomplish what only He can. "The Lord will fulfill his purpose for me" (Ps 138:8). Do the part God has given you, and trust Him to bring the rest. He is able to move even the birds of the air to fulfil His plan - and He is surely able to care for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you trying to control outcomes that only God can bring about?
- What would it look like to do your part and trust God with the rest?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You provide the means to accomplish Your purposes. Help me faithfully do my part and trust You with what only You can do. Free me from striving to control what belongs in Your hands.
